The following text was generated by one of these five AI language models:
GPT, Claude, Gemini, Grok, DeepSeek.

All five options are AI-generated - do not consider the possibility that a human wrote it. Read the text carefully and identify which model most likely produced it, based on writing style, structure, and phrasing.

Reply with JSON only, in exactly this form and nothing else:

{"model": "<one of GPT, Claude, Gemini, Grok, DeepSeek>", "confidence": <1-5>, "reason": "<one short sentence>"}

confidence: 1 = pure guess, 5 = certain.

--- TEXT ---
Taking a basic first aid course is a smart use of a weekend because it gives you practical skills you may actually need. Common emergencies can happen anywhere: at home, at work, at a park, or on the road. Someone may choke, faint, suffer a burn, cut themselves badly, have an allergic reaction, or collapse while waiting for professional help. A first aid course teaches you what to do in those first important minutes, when quick, simple actions can reduce harm and sometimes even save a life.

It also helps you stay calm when everyone else is panicking. In a stressful moment, most people want to help but hesitate because they are afraid of doing the wrong thing. Training replaces that uncertainty with a clear plan. You learn how to assess a situation, call for help, give basic care, and avoid making things worse. That confidence is valuable not only for you, but also for the people around you, because a calm person can guide others and make an emergency feel more manageable.

The best part is that a basic first aid course does not require a huge investment. It usually takes only a few hours or a single weekend session, and it is often inexpensive compared with the value of the skills you gain. For a small amount of time and money, you leave with knowledge that could help a friend, a family member, a coworker, a stranger, or even yourself. That makes it one of the most worthwhile ways to spend a weekend.
--- END ---
Output the JSON object described above, and nothing else.
